SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - SEPTEMBER 12, 2022 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

12.  Closed Session (continued)

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, reported the City Council convened into Closed Session to
  discuss Items 12A and 12B, as listed on the Closed Session agenda. The City Council
  received briefings on the aforementioned Items.

  As related to Item 12A, there was no reportable action.

  As related to Item 12B, the City Council considered the initiation of litigation pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(c)(4). The City Council decided not to initiate a
  separate case for the City, and took the following action, reported pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54957.1:

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to authorize the City
  Attorney’s Office to request of the court and to apply to participate as an amicus curiae
  or as an intervenor in the existing case, City of Redondo Beach et al. v. Bonta, in his
  capacity as California Attorney General, Los Angeles Superior Court Case No.
  22STCP01143. The substance of that case challenges the validity of Senate Bill 9 (stats.
  2021, ch. 162), mandating lot-splits or duplexes in certain single-family residential
  zones if certain conditions are met. The legal challenge alleges Senate Bill 9 violates a
  city’s charter and land use authority, among other claims (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to authorize the City
  Attorney’s Office to request of the court and to apply to participate as an amicus curiae
  in the existing case, AIDS Healthcare Foundation & City of Redondo Beach v. Bonta, in
  his capacity as California Attorney General, California Second District Court of Appeal
  Case No. B321875. The substance of that case challenges the validity of Senate Bill 10
  (stats. 2021, ch. 163), which allows but does not require city councils, by supermajority,
  to adopt ordinances enabling a process to zone parcels for up to ten units of residential
  density per parcel for “transit-rich areas” or “urban infill site,” as defined. The legal
  challenge alleges Senate Bill 10 violates a city-electorate’s voter initiative rights by
  enabling a city council to override land use limitations adopted by a voter-initiative
  ordinance. The trial court ruled in favor of Respondent Bonta, in his capacity as the
  California Attorney General. Petitioners have noticed an appeal (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  There was nothing further to report.
